BIQAI-FULL:v8p308#s079/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p308#s079/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p308#s079/r1.claim: The surah’s purpose is to establish resurrection and the gathering, displaying humanity’s final fate after the preceding surahs’ full exposition; its oaths show the matter has reached its decisive climax.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p432#2/r17.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p432#2/r17.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p432#2/r17.claim: “Go to Pharaoh” explains the call Moses received; the wording offers a gracious invitation that a reasonable person would accept.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p432#2/r17.anchor: وقوله تعالى: اذهب إلى فرعون تفسير النداء الذي ناداه به، ويحتمل أن يكون المعنى قال اذهب وفي هذه الألفاظ استدعاء حسن

JISHUMI:v10p7268/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7268/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7268/r6.claim: Ṭughyān means exceeding the limit in corruption; it parallels baghy, with related forms for the act and its agent and the nouns for transgressors.
JISHUMI:v10p7268/r6.anchor: الطغيان: مجاوزة الحد في الفنساد، طغا طغيا، فهو طاغ، ونظيره البغي، بغى يبغي، فهو باغ

JISHUMI:v10p7271/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7271/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7271/r10.claim: Jishumi argues that human acts originate from the servants themselves, citing Pharaoh's transgression, denial, turning away, and calling out.

MUQATIL:79:15-26/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:79:15-26/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:79:15-26/r4.claim: Pharaoh's transgression reached the point of making himself worshiped and calling people to worship him.
MUQATIL:79:15-26/r4.anchor: يقول: إنه قد بلغ من طغيانه أنه عبد،

MUQATIL:79:15-26/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:79:15-26/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود
MUQATIL:79:15-26/r5.claim: In Ibn Masʿūd's reading, Pharaoh had never worshiped an idol but summoned people to worship him.
MUQATIL:79:15-26/r5.anchor: وفى قراءة ابن مسعود " طغى " لأنه لم يعبد صنما قط ولكنه دعا الناس إلى عبادته،

NAHHAS:v5p143/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p143/r7.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p143/r7.claim: Those who say the present is يطغى use the past طغيت and verbal noun الطغيان; those who say يطغو use طغوت.
NAHHAS:v5p143/r7.anchor: من قال في المستقبل يطغى قال طغيت وهو الطغيان ومن قال يطغو قال طغوت

TABRISI:79:15-24/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:79:15-24/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:79:15-24/r10.claim: Pharaoh had risen in arrogance, disbelieved in God, and exceeded proper bounds in rebellion and corruption.
TABRISI:79:15-24/r10.anchor: { اذهب إلى فرعون إنه طغى } أي علا وتكبر وكفر بالله

TABATABAI:79:15-19/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:15-19/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:79:15-19/r1.claim: The account of Moses and Pharaoh warns polytheists who deny resurrection and use that denial against religious law, consoles the Prophet over rejection, and threatens his opponents.
TABATABAI:79:15-19/r1.anchor: وفيها عظة وإنذار للمشركين المنكرين للبعث وقد توسلوا به إلى رد الدعوة الدينية إذ لا معنى لتشريع الدين لولا المعاد

TABATABAI:79:15-19/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:15-19/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:79:15-19/r2.claim: The destruction of Pharaoh and his army proves Moses' divinely authorized mission; such a mission entails God's lordship over people, contrary to the polytheists' claim that lesser lords govern them.
TABATABAI:79:15-19/r2.anchor: ولا تتم رسالته من جانبه تعالى إلا بربوبية منه تعالى للناس

TABATABAI:79:15-19/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:15-19/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:79:15-19/r6.claim: The command explains the divine call; proposals to supply “saying” or an explanatory particle are unnecessary in either construction.
TABATABAI:79:15-19/r6.anchor: تفسير للنداء، وقيل الكلام على تقدير القول

TABATABAI:79:15-19/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:15-19/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:79:15-19/r7.claim: Pharaoh's transgression is the reason for the command to go to him.

BURSEVI:v10p248#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p248#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p248#2/r9.claim: The command is introduced as an implied divine utterance: “He said to him, Go to Pharaoh.”
BURSEVI:v10p248#2/r9.anchor: على إرادة القول أي فقال له اذهب إلى فرعون

BURSEVI:v10p248#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p248#2/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p248#2/r10.claim: إنه طغى explains either the command itself or why Moses must comply with it.
BURSEVI:v10p248#2/r10.anchor: تعليل للأمر أو لوجوب الامتثال به

BURSEVI:v10p248#2/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p248#2/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p248#2/r11.claim: Ṭughyān is crossing the limit: Pharaoh transgressed against God by disbelief and against people by arrogance and enslaving them; ideal servanthood instead requires truth with God and good character toward people.
BURSEVI:v10p248#2/r11.anchor: وطغى على الخلق بأ تكبر عليه واستعبدهم

BURSEVI:v10p249/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p249/r1.speaker: القاشاني
BURSEVI:v10p249/r1.claim: Al-Qāshānī says Pharaoh manifested egotism: despite strength, wisdom, and learning, he became veiled in selfhood, claimed divine attributes and lordship, and so fell into tyranny and arrogance.
BURSEVI:v10p249/r1.anchor: وقال القاشاني : أي ظهر بأنانيته وذلك إن فرعون كان ذا نفس قوية

BURSEVI:v10p249/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p249/r2.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v10p249/r2.claim: A Prophetic saying calls the worst person one upon whom the Resurrection has arrived while he is still alive; al-Qāshānī applies it to Pharaoh’s selfhood and self-worship as a veil in the station of oneness of attributes.
BURSEVI:v10p249/r2.anchor: فكان ممن قال فيه عليه السلام ، شر الناس من قامت القيامة عليه فهو حي

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:79:7-18/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:79:7-18/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:79:7-18/r8.claim: Pharaoh had exceeded the bounds through disbelief.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:79:7-18/r8.anchor: { اذهب إلى فرعون إنه طغى } جاوز الحد في الكفر.

QUSHAYRI:v3p389/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p389/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p389/r2.claim: Moses is told to go to Pharaoh because he transgressed and invite him to believe and cleanse himself of sins.
QUSHAYRI:v3p389/r2.anchor: قلنا له : { اذهب إلى فرعون إنه طغى } ، فقل له : هل يقع لك أن تؤمن وتتطهر من ذنوبك

SULAMI:v2p370#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p370#2/r1.speaker: ابن الفرحى
SULAMI:v2p370#2/r1.claim: Ibn al-Faraḥī reads the address as pointing to Pharaoh, who was himself sent to the magicians. Prophets were sent among enemies to bring God’s believing friends out from among them, not to honor those enemies.
SULAMI:v2p370#2/r1.anchor: سمعت ابن الفرحى يقول في قوله : ﴿ اذهب إلى فرعون إنه طغى ﴾ . قال : الإشارة إلى فرعون وهو المبعوث إلى السحرة

SAMIN-DURR:79:17/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:79:17/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:79:17/r1.claim: اذهب may explain the preceding call, or be governed by an elided القول (saying).
SAMIN-DURR:79:17/r1.anchor: يجوز أن يكون تفسيرا للنداء. ويجوز أن يكون على إضمار القول

SAMIN-DURR:79:17/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:79:17/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:79:17/r2.claim: A third analysis posits omitted أن, meaning أن اذهب; Abdullah's reading explicitly has أن and supports the ellipsis.
SAMIN-DURR:79:17/r2.anchor: وقيل: هو على حذف " أن " ، أي: أن اذهب. ويدل له قراءة عبد الله: " أن اذهب "

SAMIN-DURR:79:17/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:79:17/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:79:17/r3.claim: The explicit or omitted أن may be explicative or a verbal noun, with the sense that he called him to this message.
SAMIN-DURR:79:17/r3.anchor: و " أن " هذه الظاهرة أو المقدرة يحتمل أن تكون تفسيرية، وأن تكون مصدرية، أي: ناداه بكذا

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p362#2/r1.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p362#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p362#2/r1.claim: Ṭuwā is read with tanwin and kasra to resolve two adjacent sukūns, or without tanwin and with sukūn on yāʾ, as explained in Ṭā Hā.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p362#2/r1.anchor: يقرأ بالتنوين وكسره لالتقاء الساكنين وبحذف التنوين واسكان الياء وقد ذكرت علله في سورة طه

QIRAAT-ER:79:17:1#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:79:17:1#1/r1.speaker: canonical
QIRAAT-ER:79:17:1#1/r1.claim: Connected recitation drops the hamzat al-waṣl of idhhab after ṭuwā and links the place-name directly to the command.
QIRAAT-ER:79:17:1#1/r1.anchor: canonical, mutawatir: Canonical liaison from the preceding طُوَى (ṭuwā) into ٱذْهَبْ (idhhab)

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p346#3/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p346#3/r1.speaker: صخر بن جويرية
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p346#3/r1.claim: A report says Moses asked how he could go to Pharaoh when God knew Pharaoh would not respond; God told him to proceed as commanded, since twelve thousand angels in heaven seek but have not attained knowledge of destiny.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p346#3/r1.anchor: حدثني صخر ابن جويرية قال لما بعث الله موسى إلى فرعون قال ﴿ اذهب إلى فرعون إنه طغى ﴾

ALUSI-FULL:v30p29#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p29#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p29#2/r1.claim: The command may follow an implied ‘he said to him,’ explain the call itself, or be construed with an omitted explanatory أن, as in ʿAbd Allāh’s reading.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p29#2/r1.anchor: على إرادة القول والتقدير وقال له أو قائلا له اذهب الخ وقيل هو تفسير للنداء

ALUSI-FULL:v30p29#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p29#2/r2.speaker: عبد الله
ALUSI-FULL:v30p29#2/r2.claim: ʿAbd Allāh’s reading has أن before اذهب, supporting the explanatory-particle analysis.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p29#2/r2.anchor: يدل عليه قراءة عبد الله أن اذهب لأن في النداء معنى القول

ALUSI-FULL:v30p29#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p29#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p29#2/r3.claim: The clause ‘he transgressed’ gives the reason for the command or for the duty to obey it.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p29#2/r3.anchor: تعليل للأمر أو لوجوب الأمتثال به

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p328/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p328/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p328/r7.claim: Pharaoh had transgressed through arrogance, pride, and disbelief in God.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p328/r7.anchor: اذهب إلى فرعون إنه طغى} علا وتكبر وكفر بالله.

BAYDAWI-FULL:79:17-22/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:17-22/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:17-22/r1.claim: The command is understood as introducing quoted speech: Go to Pharaoh, [and say these words].
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:17-22/r1.anchor: { اذهب إلى فرعون إنه طغى } على إرادة القول

BAYDAWI-FULL:79:17-22/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:17-22/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:17-22/r2.claim: The alternative reading أن أذهب reflects the meaning of speech already contained in the address.
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:17-22/r2.anchor: وقرىء «أن أذهب» لما في النداء من معنى القول

BINTSHATI:v1p143/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p143/r6.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p143/r6.claim: Ṭughyān means exceeding a limit; in Arabic it can describe water overstepping its bounds to become dangerous.
BINTSHATI:v1p143/r6.anchor: الطغيان: تجاوز الحد، ويستعمل لغة في الماء يتجاوز الحد إلى الخطر.

BINTSHATI:v1p143/r7.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p143/r7.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p143/r7.claim: The Qur'an uses ṭughyān of water as well as human transgression; al-Ḥāqqa 69:11 says the water exceeded its bounds.
BINTSHATI:v1p143/r7.anchor: ومنه في القرآن: آية الحاقة 11: {إنا لما طغى الماء حملناكم في الجارية}

BINTSHATI:v1p143/r8.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p143/r8.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p143/r8.claim: Al-Ṭāghiya is also glossed as the flood that destroyed Thamūd.
BINTSHATI:v1p143/r8.anchor: وفسروا الطاغية كذلك بالطوفان في قوله تعالى: {فأما ثمود فأهلكوا بالطاغية}

BINTSHATI:v1p143/r9.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p143/r9.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p143/r9.claim: Most Qur'anic uses mean exceeding limits through disobedience and disbelief, as in the cited verses.
BINTSHATI:v1p143/r9.anchor: على أن أكثر استعماله القرآني، في تجاوز الحد في العصيان والكفر

BINTSHATI:v1p143/r10.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p143/r10.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p143/r10.claim: The word also describes exceeding limits through tyranny, arrogance, and oppression.
BINTSHATI:v1p143/r10.anchor: كما جاء بمعنى تجاوز الحد، في التجبر والعتو والظلم، في آيات

BINTSHATI:v1p143/r11.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p143/r11.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p143/r11.claim: The same command explains Moses' mission to Pharaoh in Ṭā Hā 20:24, where God says Pharaoh had transgressed.
BINTSHATI:v1p143/r11.anchor: وأسند الطغيان إلى فرعون موسى، في آيتي طه خطاباً لموسى

BINTSHATI:v1p144/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p144/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p144/r1.claim: The invitation echoes the command to Moses and Aaron in Ṭā Hā, including the instruction to speak gently and the hope that Pharaoh might remember or fear.
BINTSHATI:v1p144/r1.anchor: فقولا له قولاً ليناً لعله يتذكر أو يخشى

BIQAI-FULL:v8p313/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p313/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p313/r8.claim: God ordered Moses to confront Egypt's king, who enslaved Israel and feared an Israelite child; God raised Moses in Pharaoh's house as the instrument of Pharaoh's ruin, and Moses later fled after killing a man.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p313/r8.anchor: ملك مصر الذي كان استعبد بني إسرائيل ثم خوف من واحد منهم فصار يذبح أبناءهم خوفا منه وهو أنت فربيناك في بتيه لهلاكه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p313/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p313/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p313/r9.claim: Pharaoh's transgression made him liable to stern recompense; the command reassures Moses that Pharaoh has no power over him.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p313/r9.anchor: أي الحد وتجاوز الحد فاستحق المقابلة بالجد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p75/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p75/r1.speaker: ابن عامر وعاصم وحمزة والكسائي وخلف
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p75/r1.claim: The majority read Tuwa without tanwin as a feminine place-name or for one of the proposed diptote reasons; Ibn Amir, Asim, Hamza, al-Kisai, and Khalaf tanwin it as a masculine valley name.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p75/r1.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور { طوى } بلا تنوين على أنه ممنوع من الصرف للعلمية والتأنيث

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p75/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p75/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p75/r2.claim: Go to Pharaoh explains the preceding statement that his Lord called him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p75/r2.anchor: وجملة { اذهب إلى فرعون } بيان لجملة { ناداه ربه }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p75/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p75/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p75/r3.claim: The statement that Pharaoh transgressed explains the command to go; opening with inna stresses that reason.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p75/r3.anchor: وجملة { إنه طغى } تعليل للأمر في قوله : { اذهب } ، ولذلك افتتحت بحرف ( إن )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p75/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p75/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p75/r4.claim: Tughyan here means excessive arrogance, as already discussed in the description of Hell's rebellious in 78:22.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p75/r4.anchor: والطغيان إفراط التكبر وتقدم عند قوله { للطاغين مئابا في سورة النبأ

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p75/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p75/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p75/r5.claim: Pharaoh was the title of Egypt's ancient Coptic kings, a word borrowed from Hebrew; the Qur'an uses it for Moses' Egyptian king, while Joseph's ruler is called king.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p75/r5.anchor: وفرعون : لقب ملك القبط بمصر في القديم ، وهو اسم معرب عن اللغة العبرانية

NASAFI-FULL:v4p314#8/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p314#8/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p314#8/r1.claim: The command is framed with an implied saying: God tells Moses, “Go to Pharaoh.”

NASAFI-FULL:v4p314#8/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p314#8/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p314#8/r2.claim: Pharaoh exceeded the bounds through unbelief and corruption.

QURTUBI-FULL:79:15-20/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:15-20/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:79:15-20/r1.claim: The Moses story consoles Muhammad: Pharaoh was stronger than contemporary unbelievers, yet God seized him and will do likewise to them.
QURTUBI-FULL:79:15-20/r1.anchor: وهذا تسلية للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم. أي إن فرعون كان أقوى من كفار عصرك

QURTUBI-FULL:79:15-20/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:15-20/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:79:15-20/r7.claim: The call from God is omitted because a call is speech, and the text proceeds directly to the command to go.
QURTUBI-FULL:79:15-20/r7.anchor: أي ناداه ربه، فحذف، لأن النداء قول

QURTUBI-FULL:79:15-20/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:15-20/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:79:15-20/r8.claim: Pharaoh exceeded the bounds in disobedience.

QURTUBI-FULL:79:15-20/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:15-20/r9.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:79:15-20/r9.claim: Al-Hasan says Pharaoh was a non-Arab from Hamadan.
QURTUBI-FULL:79:15-20/r9.anchor: وروي عن الحسن قال: كان فرعون علجا من همدان

QURTUBI-FULL:79:15-20/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:15-20/r10.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:79:15-20/r10.claim: Mujahid says Pharaoh came from Istakhr.
QURTUBI-FULL:79:15-20/r10.anchor: وعن مجاهد قال: كان من أهل إصطخر

QURTUBI-FULL:79:15-20/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:15-20/r11.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:79:15-20/r11.claim: Another al-Hasan report places Pharaoh in Isfahan, names him Dhū Ẓufr and says he was four handspans tall.
QURTUBI-FULL:79:15-20/r11.anchor: وعن الحسن أيضا قال: من أهل أصبهان

QURTUBI-FULL:79:15-20/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:15-20/r18.speaker: صخر بن جويرية
QURTUBI-FULL:79:15-20/r18.claim: Sakhr ibn Juwayriyya reports Moses asking how to approach Pharaoh when he knew he would refuse; God ordered him to go and said twelve thousand angels seek knowledge of the decree without attaining it.
QURTUBI-FULL:79:15-20/r18.anchor: قال صخر بن جويرية: لما بعث الله موسى إلى فرعون
